cases.title: Fighters over Gold, Juno and Sword
cases.mission: Danny Browne recalled leading No. 441 Squadron RCAF on four beach patrols, starting at 06:25. The Canadian mission table records beach patrols for the squadron.
cases.effect: Browne saw the invasion fleet from above. At about 07:30, Corporal Wilfred Bennett of the Royal Winnipeg Rifles landed on Juno and described machine-gun fire from German pillboxes. Leigh-Mallory’s plan assigned 54 squadrons to beach cover.
cases.limit: The landing forces’ experience cannot isolate the protection provided by one squadron. The 54 is an allocation for a role, whereas the four are one commander’s D-Day patrols.

cases.title: Tugs delivered the assault force to the Orne bridges
cases.mission: Nos. 298 and 644 Squadrons each supplied three Halifax tugs for the six assault gliders. Their passengers included the 2nd Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire Light Infantry.
cases.effect: Five gliders landed at or near the two objectives. The RAF estimated about 140 of 170 men were immediately in action. The assault party took both bridges intact.
cases.limit: The sixth glider missed the objective. The tug crews’ releases, the gliders’ landings and the infantry’s seizure of the bridges are three distinct observations.

cases.title: Which reinforcements can be traced to a French field?
cases.mission: The 7 June transfer table identifies II./JG 3 bound for Évreux, III./JG 3 for Saint-André-de-l’Eure and IV.(Sturm)/JG 3 for Dreux. The station chronologies date the first two arrivals to 7 June and the third to 8 June. Five other Gruppen have transfer and arrival evidence in the same interval.
cases.effect: The records place named reinforcements in the western theatre after D-Day. The German June report separately counts 21 transfers over three days. It gives no names to match against the eight.
cases.limit: The eight are a lower bound from identified movements. Their presence does not establish that they flew combat immediately, confirm membership in the anonymous 21, or settle the disputed destinations of I./JG 27 and III./JG 54.

cases.title: German fighters returned to air defence as supply routes came under attack
cases.mission: The German June report describes III./SG 4 concentrating at Laval at the start of the invasion. Despite losses on the transfer, it mounted three missions on the day of arrival with four to eight aircraft per mission.
cases.effect: By 13 June German command ended bombing assignments for fighters and passed the freed formations to II. Jagdkorps. The report attributed their weakened state to Allied bombing of supply routes.
cases.limit: The German report supplies a dated change of command and role. It gives neither a target-side damage return for the three III./SG 4 missions nor an exact day for the unit’s arrival.

cases.title: Three of six German formations flew against the airborne landings
cases.mission: Luftflotte 3 ordered six formations ready for the Arnhem–Nijmegen landings. Three operated before worsening weather closed in. Caldwell identifies them as the three Gruppen of JG 26.
cases.effect: III./JG 26 encountered the 376th Fighter Squadron. Its flight leader William Beyer recalled being attacked while escorting the lift. The British landing brigade reported a quiet flight to its objectives at about 13:30.
cases.limit: Beyer’s account and the brigade report cover different positions. Caldwell attributes the absence of German fighter contact with the transports to their escorts. Individual transport saves cannot be assigned.

cases.mission: No. 48 Squadron recorded 23 departures from Down Ampney and 19 releases over landing zone S. Four gliders came down elsewhere. No. 512 Squadron towed 22 gliders with men and equipment of 1st Border.

cases.title: How much of the Arnhem resupply reached the division?
cases.mission: 49 Air Despatch Group recorded 163 aircraft off, 18 failing to return and about 377 tons dropped on 19 September.
cases.effect: The receiving division’s tables give 388 net tons dropped and 21 net tons gathered that day, or 5.4%. Its campaign accounting later recorded 106 tons collected from 1,431 dropped, with additional front-line collections only estimated.
cases.limit: The dispatch estimate and the division’s net figures have different accounting bases. The 5.4% uses the division’s own two figures. An estimated additional 100 tons for the whole operation cannot be allocated to this day.

cases.title: The Polish drop reached Driel, but the brigade found the ferry gone
cases.mission: The US 314th Troop Carrier Group carried Polish parachutists from Saltby. At 17:18, Polish brigade headquarters logged its own drop and estimated that 72 aircraft had delivered 957 troops from a dispatched force of 114 aircraft carrying 1,508.
cases.effect: At 21:00 brigade patrols reported that the ferry had sunk and the north bank was held by the enemy. At 22:30 the brigade recorded orders to reinforce the British perimeter and that it lacked the means to cross.
cases.limit: These are the brigade’s own preliminary counts for the whole lift. It reported later arrivals from off-zone drops. The figures cannot be applied to the 314th Group alone.

cases.title: Why two different Gruppen have been labelled III./JG 4
cases.mission: Nafziger’s order of battle calls the Fw 190 unit at Babenhausen III./JG 4. Holm’s separate histories locate Schröder’s II. Gruppe there and Eberle’s Bf 109-equipped III. at Darmstadt-Griesheim. Both men appear in the operational account.
cases.effect: The Dutch loss register records Fw 190s from 5. and 7./JG 4, both component Staffeln of II. Gruppe. The attack reconstruction places III. with I. on the Le Culot mission and IV. at Sint-Truiden. The separate III. Gruppe therefore remains visible alongside the evidence for II.
cases.limit: The aircraft records establish individual losses. Neither a whole Gruppe’s arrival over Le Culot nor its strength can be inferred from those two aircraft. The accounts disagree on how many reached the intended target.

cases.title: What returning Polish fighters found over Ghent
cases.mission: II./JG 1 attacked Sint-Denijs-Westrem after eight Spitfires of No. 302, twelve of No. 308 and eleven of No. 317 had left. Returning Polish pilots encountered German fighters around Ghent and Lokeren.
cases.effect: The Polish wing reported 18 Spitfires destroyed and five damaged on the ground, plus two aircraft and their pilots lost in air combat. Its pilots claimed 20 Fw 190s destroyed. Rickard gives 17 German losses for II./JG 1.
cases.limit: The 20 are claims from the Polish report. The 17 are a secondary reconstruction of German losses and include no aircraft-by-aircraft match to individual Polish pilots.

cases.title: Different airfields, different consequences in Brussels
cases.mission: I./JG 26 and III./JG 54 were sent to Grimbergen. II. and III./JG 26 were sent to Evere. Some aircraft were lost or turned back before reaching either field.
cases.effect: A member of 127 Wing’s ground crew at Evere recalled preparing four new Spitfires for squadron markings before the attack. The crew account and memorial identify engine mechanic Robert Medforth of No. 6403 Servicing Echelon as a fatal casualty there. Grimbergen, in contrast, had little aircraft traffic for its attackers to find.
cases.limit: The witness identifies the attacked field and the maintenance personnel affected. He supplies no verified serial-by-serial inventory of Evere losses, nor can he identify which German Gruppe caused Medforth’s death.

cases.title: A runway full of Typhoons at Eindhoven
cases.mission: JG 3 arrived while eight Typhoons each of RCAF Nos. 438 and 439 Squadrons were lined up to leave Eindhoven. Flight Lieutenant Peter Wilson’s No. 438 Squadron Typhoon PD556 appears in the Dutch register at the field at 09:10.
cases.effect: Rickard’s airfield total counts 60 of 125 Typhoons affected. Twenty-four were repaired locally and ten elsewhere, with 17 destroyed and nine beyond economical repair. A first damage count of 60 would overstate permanent loss.
cases.limit: The repair totals cover the field’s Typhoon force across several squadrons. They cannot be applied to the sixteen aircraft lined up or attributed to a particular JG 3 pilot.

cases.title: The 487th took off as German fighters reached Asch
cases.mission: As members of JG 11 reached Asch, the 487th Fighter Squadron was ready for takeoff. Capt. Henry Stewart described joining the fight immediately after leaving the field. Aircraft of the US 366th Fighter Group were already airborne.
cases.effect: Stewart claimed three Bf 109s destroyed. Two American pilots added supporting statements about separate combats. Rickard places about fourteen of JG 11’s aircraft losses in the battle at Asch.
cases.limit: Stewart supplied no enemy serial numbers. His three claims and the fourteen reconstructed local losses cannot be equated. The JG 11 route also took other pilots to Ophoven.

Allied.effort: Polish combat reports give 31 departures by squadron and role. US 487th Fighter Squadron testimony gives an encounter beginning at takeoff.
Allied.losses: The Polish report separates 18 Spitfires destroyed on the ground, five damaged and two lost in air combat. Eindhoven repair categories distinguish 34 repaired Typhoons from 26 destroyed or beyond repair.
Allied.effect: Returning Polish fighters engaged the attackers at Ghent. Eindhoven repairs restored part of the Typhoon force, while the Evere ground crew recorded a fatality among its mechanics.

Axis.effort: The separate II. and III./JG 4 narratives and the four JG 26/JG 54 assignments distinguish launch, intended target and reported contact.
Axis.losses: Two II./JG 4 aircraft are identified in the Dutch register. Reconstructed JG 1 losses over Ghent do not identify victims of each Polish claim.
Axis.effect: German attackers struck occupied airfields at Evere, Eindhoven and Ghent. An assigned field could be lightly occupied, as Grimbergen was, or mistaken for a different field.
